extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting to ICML 2025 and program committee members (Area Chairs, Reviewers, Program Chairs)
extracted.subtask_description: Conference-level publication ethics and review conduct guidelines for ICML 2025, covering authors' responsibilities (research ethics, authorship, originality, legal compliance), and program committee/reviewer obligations (confidentiality, conflicts, prudence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research ethics — risk identification and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: When there are risks directly associated with the proposed methods, methodology, application, or data collection and usage, authors are expected to make a reasonable effort in identifying these risks and provide a thoughtful discussion including a rationale of their decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are strongly encouraged to propose mitigation strategies for risks identified whenever feasible. It is understood that some risks—particularly those arising from general-purpose methods being applied in unforeseeable or speculative ways—may fall outside the reasonable scope of the research and need not be addressed comprehensively. (Adapted from the NeurIPS Ethics Guidelines.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrimination / Bias / Fairness concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: "Discrimination / Bias / Fairness Concerns" — Papers about applications where bias, fairness, and discrimination are a concern should acknowledge these risks and, ideally, include analysis that directly addresses the relevant area of concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: hiring algorithms — include analysis that is feasible and within a reasonable scope to address bias/fairness concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate potential applications & impact (human rights etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Inappropriate Potential Applications & Impact (e.g., human rights concerns)" — Papers about applications that have a direct connection to human rights issues should provide a thoughtful discussion of the risks of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate and within the scope of the work, authors may also suggest reasonable recommendations for mitigating these risks (e.g., when research could be applied to weapons or other harmful domains).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible research practices (IRB, consent, documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Responsible Research Practice (e.g., IRB, documentation, research ethics, participant consent)" — Research involving human subjects should provide evidence that it adhered to the authors’ home institution’s procedures for obtaining IRB approval or was eligible for an exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guideline acknowledges that IRB standards vary across borders and institutions; authors should document approvals or eligibility for exemption where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and security (personally identifiable information)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Privacy and Security (e.g., personally identifiable information)" — Papers that rely on data that includes personally identifiable information should make reasonable efforts to ensure that individuals are not identifiable in the research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should describe steps taken to protect privacy and secure sensitive data; reasonable de-identification and minimization measures are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal compliance (GDPR, EU AI Act, copyright, terms of use)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Legal Compliance (e.g., EU AI Act, GDPR, copyright, terms of use)" — ICML is international; where appropriate, papers should provide evidence that local laws and regulations were followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific issues called out include: addressing fair use of copyrighted material for training generative models, and ensuring compliance with the EU AI Act where applicable. The page lists categories of AI systems banned by the EU AI Act (e.g., subliminal manipulation, exploiting vulnerabilities, biometric categorization, untargeted scraping to create facial recognition databases, certain real-time biometric collection for law enforcement, workplace/education emotion inference except for medical/safety reasons). Authors using relevant datasets or building systems in these areas should acknowledge and address legal risks in the impact statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research integrity issues (plagiarism, collusion, fabrication)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Research Integrity Issues (e.g., plagiarism, collusion rings, etc.)" — Issues in this category will bypass the ethics review process and be escalated to the Program Chairs for adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flagged integrity problems are treated as serious misconduct and handled by higher-level program leadership rather than the standard ethics-review flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship (who to list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should comprise exactly those individuals who made a significant contribution to the research; other contributors should be acknowledged upon acceptance in the final camera-ready submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submitting author must ensure that all co-authors have seen and approved the final manuscript and have agreed to its submission for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitted paper is entirely written by the authors of the paper. If the work of others has been used, that work must be properly cited or quoted. Publications that have significantly influenced the nature of the work must be cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only relevant publications should be cited and self-citation should be kept to a minimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Dual submission rules apply as described in the call for papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must consult the call for papers for the specific prohibitions/requirements around submitting the same or substantially overlapping work to multiple venues; violating those rules can lead to rejection or sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud and correctness (fabrication, errors, corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraudulent or knowingly inaccurate statements are unacceptable, including but not limited to the use of fabricated data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, before publication of the final version, an author discovers a significant error or inaccuracy in the submitted paper, the author must promptly notify the program chairs and either retract the paper or correct it if feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author conflict of interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial or any other substantive conflict of interest that might be construed to influence the results or interpretation of the manuscript must be disclosed to the program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon acceptance, information pertaining to the conflict must be made available in the final version, including all sources of financial support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program committee aims and goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The program committee (Program Chairs, Senior Area Chairs, Area Chairs, Reviewers) must strive to meet the expectations/needs of conference participants, readers and authors: a high quality and intellectually stimulating program and a fair and professional review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the standard for PC conduct and prioritizes both program quality and fairness to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All information pertaining to individual submitted manuscripts must be kept confidential by program committee members and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members and reviewers must protect the authors' ideas and not disclose or misuse confidential manuscript information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must be evaluated only for their contents, as explained on the review form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should avoid extraneous considerations (e.g., author identity) and focus on scientific content, validity, originality, clarity, and impact per the review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence / reporting guideline violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must bring to the attention of the Area Chair handling a paper any information that may be a reason to reject the submitted paper, such as the violation of these guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer notices suspected ethical/legal/integrity violations, they should escalate promptly rather than ignore them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program committee conflicts of interest and recusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Program committee members must disclose any conflicts of interest through OpenReview (or, for reviewers, notify the cognizant Area Chair; for Area Chairs, notify the cognizant Senior Area Chair). Any program committee member who is conflicted with a paper due to close ties to the authors cannot participate in deciding the fate of that paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Chairs are not exempt; if a Program Chair is conflicted, non-conflicted Program Chairs must make decisions without involvement of the conflicted chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subversive hidden LLM prompts are misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting a paper with a "hidden" prompt intended to obtain a favorable review from an LLM is scientific misconduct; the inclusion of such a prompt is an attempt to subvert the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is distinct from hidden prompts intended to detect if reviewers are using LLMs (the latter is acceptable). The page notes that ICML 2025 identified some submissions with such hidden prompts, contacted the authors, and reported cases to oversight bodies rather than desk-rejecting in all cases.
